title: A 401 or 403 that is not about the API key
evidence: Stated by Plorea 2026-10-13; the cross-environment 404 observed in production the same day
note: Since 2026-10-13 the API key sets the environment (plr_test_ or plr_live_). An X-Environment header that does not match the key returns 403 (AuthenticationException). A live key with PLOREA_ENVIRONMENT unset sends "test" and gets 403 on every call. Check the variable before you rotate the key. Run check-setup: it compares the key prefix with the environment.

source.heading: A 401 or 403 that is not about the API key

title: 404: unknown reference, or an id from the other environment
evidence: VERIFIED (open link 200, unknown reference 404); cross-environment 404 observed in production 2026-10-13
note: payments/status answers 200 for an open, never-paid link. Only a reference Plorea does not know answers 404. An id created in the other environment (test vs live) also answers 404. Treat NotFoundException as a normal answer to "does this exist?", not as an outage.

title: 400 and 402 on a subscription charge mean different things
note: 402 (ChargeFailedException) is a card decline and nothing else: start dunning, the subscription is fine. 400 (ValidationException) means the subscription is not chargeable at all: it is cancelled, or its payment method is not active. Your app sent a request it should not have.

title: Validation messages are static templates
note: A request that misses two required fields answers with a list of all five. Log the message and show it to a developer. Never parse it, and never show it to a customer as a list of what to fix.

title: 409 with paidUntil on a subscription update
note: A subscription update whose new nextChargeAt is inside a paid period answers 409 with paidUntil. The SDK throws NextChargeInPaidPeriodException; paidUntil() returns the period end. Send allowEarlyCharge() to charge anyway. A 409 without paidUntil is a plain RequestException.

title: Retries can bill twice
evidence: VERIFIED (duplicate references create two live links); Idempotency-Key VERIFIED broken 2026-11-09 (test)
note: POST payments/link, subscription creation and subscriptions()->charge() have no idempotency. A retry can create a second live link or a second charge. Keep PLOREA_RETRY_TIMES=0, use firstOrCreate() for payment links, and reconcile by reading state back. A timeout is not a failure: it is an unknown, so re-read state before you decide. refund() and cancel() are safe to retry with the same modificationReference. API 0.31 documents an Idempotency-Key header, but in test on 2026-11-09 a repeated key created a second row and moved nextChargeAt, and a reused key with a different amount was booked as authorised. Do not rely on it; the SDK does not send it.

title: firstOrCreate() refuses a reference that is already paid
note: firstOrCreate() throws PaymentAlreadyPaidException when the reference is already paid. $e->status holds the settled PaymentStatus. The SDK refuses on purpose: a fresh link for a settled invoice makes it payable twice.

title: A refused payment reports "failed", never "refused"
note: A declined payment reads status "failed" with webhookEventCode AUTHORISATION and webhookSuccess false. The string "refused" never appears, so $status->is('refused') is dead code. The webhook type is payment.failed, never payment.refused. Status bodies seen since 2026-10-06 also carry refusalReason; read it from $status->raw.

title: "expired" is never reported: links stay open
note: A link past its expiry keeps reporting an open status. Judge expiry from the expiresAt returned at creation, or from the pay page's computed expired flag. The status string will not tell you.

source.heading: ✅ `expired` is never reported — links stay "open" forever

title: Refunds and cancellations settle in hours, not minutes
evidence: VERIFIED 2026-09-09 (more than 11 hours in test); final statuses stated by Plorea 2026-09-21; subscription-charge refunds VERIFIED 2026-10-19 (test)
note: Payment links: refund_requested and cancel_requested mean accepted. They can last more than 11 hours. Poll on a scale of hours, or wait for the webhook. Never tell a customer a refund failed, and never reverse it in your books, on a timeout alone. A payment link has no per-refund status field: persist the Refund DTO, because refundPspReference exists only on the refund response. Subscription charges are different (verified 2026-10-19, test): status() on the {subscriptionId}-{chargeId} reference returns a refunds list with a status and settledAt per refund, and no payment.refunded webhook arrived, so poll status(). Never cancel a charged subscription charge: refund it.

title: Plorea never redelivers a failed webhook
note: A delivery that fails is not sent again, so answering 500 loses the event. Store each delivery before you process it, queue the work, and answer fast. Run a scheduled backstop that re-reads open payments, pending card setups and subscriptions()->needingAttention(): card setup, cancel and reactivate emit no webhook at all.

title: The webhook signature covers the raw body only
note: x-plorea-signature is base64(HMAC-SHA256(secret, raw body)). The headers sit outside the signature, so deduplicate on $event->eventId, which the SDK reads from the signed body. A middleware that re-encodes the body before AuthenticateWebhook breaks the HMAC while the payload still looks valid. The signing secret is not the API key and not the tenant id.

title: A failed scheduled charge: past_due is not overdue
note: After a failed scheduled charge the subscription reads past_due, retryCount 1 and a failureReason. nextChargeAt moves to the failure time plus retryIntervalDays, so a past_due subscription does not look overdue. needingAttention() checks the status as well as the date. One subscription.charge_failed is sent per attempt.

title: After the last retry: payment_failed, not canceled
evidence: VERIFIED in production 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-08; the transitions out are mostly untested
note: After three failed attempts about 24 hours apart, the subscription reads payment_failed, retryCount 3 and nextChargeAt null. It is not canceled. PATCH with status active answers 400. cancel() works. The verified way back to billing is a new subscription on the same payment method. charges() is not reliably newest first: sort by createdAt.

title: A failed card setup is terminal, and failureReason is null
note: A payment method goes pending_setup, then active or failed. failed is terminal: no card was stored and no retry of that method can succeed. failureReason is null even for a genuine refusal, so branch on status alone.

title: A payment method in use cannot be deleted
note: paymentMethods()->delete() answers 400 while subscriptions still use the method. The SDK throws PaymentMethodInUseException, which extends ValidationException; activeSubscriptionIds() lists the subscriptions that block it.

title: Amounts are minor units (øre)
note: 10000 is 100,00 kr. The API has no major-unit representation anywhere.

title: A refund over the remaining amount is a 400
triggers: Refund amount exceeds original payment amount
note: refund() with more than is left answers 400 with originalAmount, alreadyRefunded, requestedAmount and remainingAmount. The SDK throws RefundAmountExceededException (extends ValidationException). Before API 0.31 the same refusal was a 422. Ask first: payments()->status($reference)->canRequestRefund() and ->refundable->remainingAmount.

title: Cancel on a captured payment or charge is a 409
evidence: VERIFIED 2026-11-09 (test), API 0.31; before that the cancel was accepted and Adyen refused it (2026-10-19)
note: payments()->cancel() on a captured payment answers 409 "Payment has been captured; use /payments/refund"; on a subscription charge "Charge has been captured; use refund". The SDK throws PaymentAlreadyCapturedException for both. Match on the class, not the message. Refund instead.

title: Cancel on an unpaid link withdraws it
note: payments()->cancel() on an unpaid link answers status cancelled with paymentLinkId, amount and cancelledAt (isLinkWithdrawn() is true). A second cancel answers the same with alreadyCancelled true. After that the pay page answers 410 and payments/session 400, both with cancelledAt: PaymentLinkCancelledException.

title: Onboarding a company another partner owns is a 409
triggers: Merchant is onboarded by another partner
evidence: VERIFIED 2026-11-09 (live), one company; payout destination UNOBSERVED
note: merchants()->onboard()->save() for a company that another Plorea partner already onboarded answers 409 with merchantOrgNr. Nothing is created and no KYC e-mail is sent. The SDK throws MerchantOnboardedByAnotherPartnerException. merchants()->find() answers 404 for the same company, so a 404 does not mean the company is free. A payment link with that org number is still created and its pay page opens. Which balance account receives the money is not observed: ask Plorea before you sell for such a merchant.

title: A merchant without a store is never charged
evidence: Observed in live 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-09; partners endpoint VERIFIED 2026-11-09 (live read)
note: A live subscription for a merchant org number with approved KYC but no store was never charged: the scheduler moved nextChargeAt once and stopped. Read Plorea::merchants()->find($orgNr) first. isReadyForPayments() needs KYC approved, a storeId and ready card methods. needsKycAction() and kycProblems() say what the merchant must fix. The endpoint answers in live only.
